plausible_interpretations_considered.definition: sqrt(sum of squared hourly log returns across each exact prior h-hour window)
plausible_interpretations_considered.assessment: Uses the same realized-volatility object and units as the frozen future target; directly honors the frozen 1/24/168/720-hour cardinalities and requires no unregistered daily resampling. It includes completed hour t and is backward-looking only.

plausible_interpretations_considered.definition: Average a base-period realized measure over the prior h hourly periods
plausible_interpretations_considered.assessment: HAR literature commonly averages lower-frequency realized-volatility components, but the frozen contract supplies hourly data and an hourly-contiguous future RV target. Averaging hourly RVs would change the scale and aggregation object; averaging squared returns would produce variance units and require an unregistered square-root convention.

plausible_interpretations_considered.definition: Use log realized volatility or realized variance as baseline regressors
plausible_interpretations_considered.assessment: Materially changes the frozen benchmark metric and introduces a transform not specified by the census; not selected.

scientific_rationale: The selected construction is the smallest deterministic completion of the frozen phrase 'prior 1-hour, 24-hour, 168-hour, and 720-hour realized-volatility aggregates'. It preserves volatility units and the square-root-of-squared-log-return object used by the frozen future target, while avoiding an unregistered resampling or transform. The choice is outcome blind and is not asserted to be uniquely correct in general.

primary_literature_used.citation: Corsi (2009), A Simple Approximate Long-Memory Model of Realized Volatility, Journal of Financial Econometrics 7(2), 174-196
primary_literature_used.relevance: HAR-RV uses realized-volatility components at heterogeneous horizons.

primary_literature_used.citation: Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold and Labys (2003), Modeling and Forecasting Realized Volatility, Econometrica 71(2), 579-625
primary_literature_used.relevance: Realized volatility is constructed from sums of squared high-frequency returns and used for volatility modeling/forecasting.

hourly_return.timestamp_definition: u is a UTC hourly close boundary; C_u is the close of the completed kline [u-1h,u].
hourly_return.validity: C_(u-1) and C_u must be finite and strictly positive; otherwise the candidate fails closed.

HAR_1H_t.boundaries: (t-1h,t], includes hour t, maximum timestamp t

HAR_24H_t.boundaries: (t-24h,t], includes hour t, maximum timestamp t

HAR_168H_t.boundaries: (t-168h,t], includes hour t, maximum timestamp t

HAR_720H_t.boundaries: (t-720h,t], includes hour t, maximum timestamp t

leakage_proof.proof: Every baseline return ends at a close boundary no later than t; the target starts with r_(t+1h), so no baseline return is in the future target and no target return is in a baseline term.
leakage_proof.synthetic_example: For t=2020-01-02T00:00:00Z, HAR_1H ends with C_t and uses (t-1h,t]; HAR_24H begins at C_(t-24h) and ends at C_t; RV24_future begins with (t,t+1h] and ends at (t+23h,t+24h].

materialization_compatibility.structural_reason: Manifest metadata shows the first JFP03 raw timestamp is 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z and the last is 2024-12-31T23:00:00Z. The first scheduled decision t=2020-01-01T00:00:00Z requires C_(t-720h)=2019-12-02T00:00:00Z for HAR_720H_t, which is absent. The last scheduled decision t=2024-12-31T23:00:00Z requires future closes through t+24h=2025-01-01T23:00:00Z, which are also absent. The 60-object snapshot therefore lacks both required support regions.
materialization_compatibility.additional_structural_requirement: At least contiguous BTCUSDT USD-M 1h source coverage sufficient to provide all closes from C_(2020-01-01T00:00:00Z-720h) through C_(2024-12-31T23:00:00Z+24h), with the same checksum, schema, timestamp, and continuity contract.
